# v0.16.26 — Nested validation scratch

## Changes

- Resolve explicitly configured validation scratch relative to the individual check's working directory, including a nested checkout. Generated scratch no longer invalidates that check solely because its directory differs from the Location.
- Continue to protect declared inputs, tracked inputs, and exact outputs. Refresh and Review rediscover tracked inputs for the captured validation working directory, including newly tracked files; older bindings keep their original scratch recipe.
- Reuse the scoped tracked-file discovery from #384 and disable `core.fsmonitor` for those scans. A Git subdirectory Location still scans its own tracked files even when its `.git` is in an ancestor.

The execution recovery, validation evidence, Coordinator default and concise reports from #384 were already delivered in #385 and v0.16.25; they are not reapplied here. The older stale-evidence record did not retain a per-file snapshot diff, so this change does not establish its unique cause.

## Review disposition and deferred work

- #384's tracked-file protection finding for a Git subdirectory Location is valid; the Location scan is retained and covered alongside the nested-checkout cases.
- Its fsmonitor finding applies to the introduced tracked-file scans; the existing #384 override is included for these scans, without claiming to secure all Git operations.
- The `.git/info/attributes` compatibility finding concerns #384's private filterless Review implementation, which is not included here; that implementation's behavior is neither adopted nor claimed fixed.
- The redirected-metadata and nested Git Review content findings, the recursive submodule/filterless Review work, and broader Git hardening remain deferred. The user did not request that work as a condition of this integration. The pre-existing behavior and the synthetic reproduction described in the v0.16.25 notes are not claimed fixed.

## Release identity

The Mission runtime asset marker is `0.16.26-nested-validation-scratch-v1`. After integration, fix the `main` commit and a single SHA-256-pinned archive for candidate preflight, full validation, applicable CI, CLI Worker startup, installation and distribution. Worker startup is not task completion or an official score. npm publication is a separate manual step; an installed marker alone does not prove that a running host has reloaded it.

# v0.16.25 — Execution and validation recovery

## Changes

- Recover eligible predecessor execution evidence and reconcile native terminal state, validation binding and writer ownership without forcibly releasing a live or unknown owner.
- Keep validation scratch exclusions tied to the individual check and preserve declared and Location-tracked inputs. A cwd-relative scratch exclusion not present in the earlier Location-relative recipe is deferred, so generated files in such a nested checkout may make a check stale.
- Recognize quoted Git identity values without weakening command-boundary checks.
- Default the Mission Coordinator to Terra while retaining explicit model overrides and existing role configuration.
- Keep the normal return report concise while retaining its summary, cost and history caveats, and internal records.

The historical stale-evidence record did not retain a per-file snapshot diff, so its unique cause is not established. Execution recovery does not establish completion or official grading of an external task.

## Deferred Git behavior

This candidate retains the published Location-only snapshot Git scan rather than the new nested-checkout scan, and does not include the later recursive submodule Review implementation. The earlier Review path for ordinary nested Git checkouts remains. A synthetic run with a writable nested checkout and its `.git` redirected to another host-readable repository produced that repository's tracked content in `missionReviewSource`'s excerpt in v0.16.24. Actual host permission bypass, real secret disclosure and external transmission were not established by that internal-function reproduction. The collection behavior and broader Git-boundary work remain for follow-up; this is not a claim that the behavior is safe.

## Release identity and validation

The Mission runtime asset marker is `0.16.25-execution-recovery-v1`. Record the integrated `main` commit and one SHA-256-pinned archive for candidate preflight, full validation, Linux/Windows CI and actual CLI Worker startup. Worker startup is not task completion or an official score. Use the same fixed archive for installations and the GitHub Release; npm publication is a separate manual step. An installed marker does not prove that a running OpenCode host has reloaded the plugin; verify its loaded path and marker after a manual restart.

# v0.16.24 — Prelaunch scope recovery

## Changes

- Recover an operation rejected before launch after an effective scope correction, while recording call-, run- and input-bound host receipts and preventing duplicate admission.
- Reconcile native history, including concurrent status reads, unavailable history and contradictory process evidence, without treating a tool envelope or error text as proof that a process started or did not start.
- Resolve a limited initial prefix of immutable PowerShell path definitions without evaluating expressions. Preserve literal-dollar paths and reject unresolved destinations after pipelines, executable prefixes or engine-owned variable assignments.
- Bind the isolated prelaunch-recovery CLI scenario to its actual direct root executor and model; a Worker dispatch is not accepted as that scenario's direct execution.

These changes do not recover another owner's live operation or establish completion or grading of an external task.

## Release identity and validation

The intended runtime asset marker is `0.16.24-prelaunch-scope-recovery-v1`. Record the integrated `main` commit and SHA-256-pinned archive alongside candidate preflight, full validation, Linux/Windows CI, independent review, and actual CLI Worker startup. Startup is not task completion or an official score. Install and publish the same fixed archive. An installed marker does not prove that a running OpenCode host has reloaded the plugin; verify its loaded path and marker after a manual restart.

# v0.16.23 — Timed operation boundary correction

## Changes

- Reject additional shell commands and input redirections appended to a declared timed operation, including LF and CRLF boundaries. This corrects an operation-observation gap in v0.16.22.
- Preserve existing matching for valid timed operations, declared redirects, failure results, and observation ownership. The fix covers the public Mission tool hook and both plain and explicitly timed declarations.
- The change does not recover uncollected operations from other owners or runs and does not establish recovery of the original live operation.

## Release identity and validation

The intended runtime asset marker is `0.16.23-operation-boundary-v1`. Record the integrated `main` commit and SHA-256-pinned archive alongside candidate preflight, full validation, Linux/Windows CI, and actual CLI Worker startup. Startup is not task completion or an official score. Install and publish the same fixed archive. An installed marker does not prove that a running OpenCode host has reloaded the plugin; verify its loaded path and marker after a manual restart.

releases.name: v0.16.22 — Timed operation observation
releases.body:
# v0.16.22 — Timed operation observation

## Changes

- Recognize the literal POSIX `TIMEFORMAT='<ASCII_IDENTIFIER>=%R'; time <command>` envelope when reconciling a native operation, without accepting a different command, output redirection, working directory or arbitrary shell wrapper.
- Retain an already collected operation observation across a unique equivalent declaration in the same working directory. Original ownership, terminal and exit remain attached to the observation; a bare Node declaration cannot prove that a different pinned binary ran.
- Classify `NO_START` and structured failure output separately from the recognized envelope's trailing duration, without changing the native output or exit.
- The change does not import an uncollected call from another owner or run, and does not establish recovery of the original live operation. The regression tests cover the V2 history projection and public Mission APIs, not a replay of that operation.

## Release identity and validation

The intended runtime asset marker is `0.16.22-operation-elapsed-v1`. Record the integrated `main` commit and SHA-256-pinned archive with the candidate preflight, full validation, Linux/Windows CI and actual CLI Worker startup separately; a startup is not completion or an official score. Use the same fixed archive for installation and publication. An installed marker does not prove that an already-running OpenCode host reloaded the plugin; verify the loaded path and marker after a manual restart.
